body:
AMEND — codex-component-ledger-review, independent read-only review under the anti-dither rule.

C1-T is finite: one exact public inventory plus a closed constructor/refusal/mutation matrix, followed by A–F. The global court precedes every production type, each child owns the laws for the types it introduces, only F closes aggregate C1, and the scope/authority exclusions remain correct. I find no representability, scientific-conflation, or reproducibility defect in the A–F allocation itself.

One concrete constructibility defect remains in the stated exit condition. “One constructor/refusal/mutation witness for every D2/C1 rule,” together with unspecified “outside-package construction probes,” does not require all independent Scala construction doors to be tested. A relational type can refuse ordinary apply and copy yet remain forgeable through companion fromProduct or summon[Mirror.ProductOf[T]].fromProduct; a probe can also pass vacuously when the mechanism itself is unavailable. That is the exact failure class already measured in current core.

Narrow repair: make C1-T’s finite matrix enumerate, for every non-Cartesian/checked public type, (1) every declared public or package-visible factory including any unsafe-named path, (2) apply, (3) copy, (4) companion fromProduct, and (5) Mirror.ProductOf.fromProduct. Every compile-refusal mechanism needs its own same-mechanism positive control. Honest Cartesian-product records may mark a door intentionally open; relational values must close it or route through a checked constructor. Each C1 child then instantiates those predeclared rows when its type lands.

With that exact repair, ACCEPT. This adds no ontology, implementation slice, provider preference, or new court cycle; it makes the already-promised closed type court actually discriminate forgeable values.
